key_insight: LoRA factor gradients cannot detect task-relevant directions normal to the current low-rank manifold, while the normal spectrum reveals the local value of expanding rank.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-aware rank expansion can improve fine-tuning accuracy while using fewer trainable parameters than capacity-allocation approaches.
method: Optimize existing degrees of freedom using tangent-space information.
Estimate the normal spectrum matrix-free and expand along leading singular directions.
Initialize new capacity using task-induced geometry.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports best average performance across evaluated language and vision settings; on LLaMA3-8B, average commonsense score rises from 86.61 to 88.45 while trainable parameters fall from 42.0M to 14.4M.
watch_item: Rank-expansion optimality assumes a local quadratic model; the abstract does not quantify normal-spectrum estimation overhead.
paper_title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA
